name: password-policy-input
title: Password Policy Input
description: Password policy editor that checks rules against NIST SP 800-63B-4 (composition rules, forced rotation, security questions, hints, minimum under 15 or 8 with MFA, maximum under 64, blocked paste, no breach check or attempt limit), shows sample passwords and applies defaults.

meta.stops: Helps catch password rules that weaken accounts
meta.summary: Reads an admin's password rules back against NIST SP 800-63B-4 and shows what they do to real passwords, so the rules don't make accounts weaker.
meta.server: Enforce length, blocklist and attempt limits in your authentication service.
catches: Composition rules (mixtures of character types), which NIST says SHALL NOT be imposed
Minimum under 15 (or 8 when only used with MFA), maximum under 64
Paste blocked, no breached-password check, no failed-attempt limit
What the rules accept and refuse, shown on sample passwords
limits: Covers the password sections of the standard, not the whole of SP 800-63B
Doesn't enforce anything; your auth system applies the policy
a11y: Every policy input has a visible label, aria-invalid on SHALL findings and a description
Fix buttons are real buttons; focus moves to the summary after applying defaults

sources.label: NIST SP 800-63B-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management

rules.note: Informational; check the official source. Confirmed: minimum 15 for single-factor, 8 when only used with MFA; SHOULD permit at least 64; SHALL NOT impose composition rules, periodic change, hints or KBA; SHOULD permit paste.
